attrs.evidence: derive_realm_battery.mjs case 'multiplicity-preserves-correlation' drives two authority-driven executions of ONE issued request across a change to derive_worker.mjs's bytes -- same catalog, same family, same request, same result -- and requires acceptance to report two correlated execution_observations, executable_artifact_id null because it is not unique, each session still attached to the artifact that actually ran it, and executor_sessions of length 2. Restoring the list[0] form fails the case. The witness restores the worker's bytes in a finally block, so the artifact tree is unchanged whether it passes or throws.
attrs.statement: MULTIPLICITY MUST PRESERVE CORRELATION. EVIDENCE FIELDS THAT VARY TOGETHER MAY NOT BE INDEPENDENTLY COLLAPSED INTO SINGULAR SUMMARIES. Round 24 established that the observation key is over BYTES, so two launches producing byte-identical output share it, and made executor_sessions plural so that one id would stop being reported as though it named the launch in hand. It left executable_artifact_id singular over that same plural list, taking list[0]. Those two fields are not independent. Run one issued request, append a comment to derive_worker.mjs, run it again: the host honestly observes S1 -> artifact A -> 5 and S2 -> artifact B -> 5, and the old shape reported executable_artifact_id A beside executor_sessions [S1, S2], implying both sessions ran A. Nothing false is accepted and no execution is invented -- both happened and both produced these exact request/result bytes -- so this is not a forgery but a PROVENANCE SHAPE defect, and it matters because the two artifact versions may differ arbitrarily and coincide only on this request's result. It is the database error of selecting one column from the first row and another column from all rows and presenting the pair as a record. THE TUPLE IS THE UNIT: observations are grouped by the (implementation_family_id, executable_artifact_id) that actually co-occurred, carrying the sessions that ran it, and every singular field is DERIVED -- emitted only when genuinely unique and null otherwise, which is what the family id has done since round 24 and what the artifact id should have done alongside it. Provenance is RELATIONAL: family <-> artifact <-> session, not three unrelated sets. There is ONE summariser, in the host, used by the host and by the authority that merges across invocations, because the first version of that merge rewrote the same correlation bug one level up.
